To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the mean systolic blood pressure in 24-h ambulatory blood pressure recordings is higher than that in clinic measurements, and the diurnal pattern of ambulatory blood pressure is similar to that in clinic measurements; (2) the 24-h mean diastolic blood pressure is similar in ambulatory blood pressure and clinic measurements; and (3) the mean 24-h heart rate is higher in ambulatory blood recordings than in clinic measurements.

ambulatory blood pressure is a better predictor of cardiovascular events than conventional blood pressure measurements, and that ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring should be used for diagnosis and treatment decisions in hypertension and in other conditions in which blood pressure is a risk factor.

ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) monitoring in a large population of untreated subjects with normal office BP (OBP), defined as <140/90 mm Hg, revealed a high prevalence of hypertension and that ABP was more predictive of cardiovascular events than OBP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the ambulatory blood pressure and the comparison of this parameter with other measurements of blood pressure.
the study of the relationship between blood pressure and age in a group of healthy people.
the study of the normality of blood pressure in the ambulatory setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 24-hr blood pressure is not the best indicator of the risk of hypertension, and that the ambulatory blood pressure measurement is the most accurate method of assessing the risk of hypertension.
ambulatory blood pressure is not a substitute for office blood pressure measurement but is a useful adjunct.
ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is not a substitute for the measurement of blood pressure in the clinic, but is a complementary tool for the evaluation of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 24 hour average blood pressure is not a good predictor of the risk of cardiovascular events.
the ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) measurement, when compared with other methods, is a reliable and accurate method for the diagnosis of hypertension.
the ambulatory measurement of blood pressure (BP) has been shown to be a reliable and useful technique for assessing the cardiovascular risk in patients with hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ambulatory blood pressure (BP) monitoring is an important tool for assessing cardiovascular risk and that it should be considered as part of routine clinical care.
